fact: The director of addressing at the Ministry of Construction, Housing and Urban Planning said on 30 September 2025 that addressing of the Abidjan district (about 17,000 roads identified, 500,000 entities to receive addresses, FCFA 12bn project financed by the World Bank and the State) is due to finish on 31 December 2025 and is being duplicated nationally, with about fifteen cities to be addressed by 2030.

The Ministry of Construction, Housing and Urban Planning says the Abidjan street addressing project met on 4-5 April 2024 to begin effective implementation of the address database, presented as the official address reference.

fact: A data-sharing framework agreement for the Abidjan District addressing project (PADA) was signed on 24 January 2023, to give addresses and name all streets across the district's 13 communes (AIP).

AIP reports that BNETD, through its addressing centre, launched the Projet d'adressage des villes de l'intérieur (PAVI) in Daloa on 15 January 2025, a three-year pilot of field surveys, door and street numbering and street-name signs, which also covers Bouaké and Korhogo.

fact: Abidjan Planet reports the Abidjan district addressing project (PADA, launched 2021) has named 14,276 streets, laid 25,750 of 87,914 street signs (laying suspended in November 2025 to fix defects) and fitted 290,805 door plates (95%), while the PAVI project extends addressing to Yamoussoukro, Bouake, Korhogo and Daloa.

The Direction Generale de l'Economie says the Abidjan addressing project (PADA) has street and unit marking under way in all five zones, over 15,000 street names approved, the Google Maps addressing system effective in zones 1 and 2 and unit plaques completed there.

The Direction Generale de l'Economie says the interior-cities addressing project (PAVI), launched in 2023, had by end June 2025 surveyed 26,840 units in Yamoussoukro, 69,188 in Korhogo and 61,779 in Daloa.

fact: IGN FI says the Abidjan District Addressing Project (PADA) completed 217,000 occupancy-unit surveys and applied 146,000 numbering marks between November 2021 and October 2023, towards an addressing system for the Abidjan district.
